title: Quantum algorithm for Valiant-Vazirani reduction
authors: Patrick Kelly, Victoria S. Ordonez, Michael R. Geller
abstract: There is growing interest in extensions of the standard model of gate-based quantum computation to include auxiliary degrees of freedom evolving according to a nonlinear Schrödinger equation. By reducing the Boolean satisfiability problem SAT to quantum state discrimination, Abrams and Lloyd argued that the right type of nonlinearity can be used to solve {\sf NP} and \#{\sf P} problems in polynomial time, at least in an idealized noise-free limit. For practical implementation, however, we are restricted to simulated and emergent nonlinearities, such as that appearing in mean field models for ultracold atoms and similar ensembles. A prominent example is the torsion model, which arises in two-component Bose-Einstein condensates and spin models with all-to-all Ising interaction. But torsion-based state discrimination appears to fall short of solving SAT. Here we close this gap by constructing the filtered oracle of the Valiant-Vazirani theorem, providing a randomized polynomial-time reduction from SAT to UNIQUE SAT, a promise problem where there is at most 1 satisfying assignment. In the noise free limit, the UNIQUE SAT problem can be olved in polynomial time using torsion nonlinearity. Quantum Valiant-Vazirani reduction is no faster than the efficient classical version, but a fault-tolerant implementation coupled to a nonlinear quantum coprocessor simulating torsion would enable polynomial time solution to {\sf NP} (but not \#{\sf P}) problems.
summary: The paper develops a quantum algorithm implementing the Valiant-Vazirani reduction by transforming SAT into UNIQUE SAT. This is achieved by constructing a complex oracle circuit based on random hashing constraints and leveraging 'torsion nonlinearity' found in systems like Bose-Einstein condensates. The result suggests that fault-tolerant implementation could solve NP problems, though this speedup requires nonlinear quantum hardware.
main_problem: To construct a quantum algorithm for the Valiant-Vazirani reduction, which reduces the NP-complete SAT problem to UNIQUE SAT.
main_result: The authors provide a randomized polynomial-time reduction from SAT to UNIQUE SAT using a filtered oracle. This implies that fault-tolerant implementation could solve NP problems in polynomial time via nonlinear quantum coprocessors.
method: The core method involves constructing a filtered Boolean function $\phi(x)$ by combining the original 3SAT formula with indicator functions derived from random hash constraints, which are then implemented using reversible oracle circuits.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework relies on extending gate-based quantum computation to include auxiliary degrees of freedom governed by a nonlinear Schrödinger equation. The specific nonlinearity utilized is 'torsion nonlinearity,' arising in models like two-component Bose-Einstein condensates or spin systems with all-to-all Ising interaction.
key_observables: The probability $p = 	ext{Pr}(X=1)$ of finding the unique satisfying assignment, and the expected number of solutions $\lambda$.
important_parameters: The analysis requires choosing an optimal hash dimension $k$ such that $1/16 < \lambda \le 1/8$, and the speedup is contingent on operating in the noise-free limit.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions are the existence of a fault-tolerant nonlinear quantum coprocessor simulating torsion, and the analysis holds strictly in the idealized noise-free limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Valiant-Vazirani filter concept using random partitioning, circuits for encoding hash constraints (8 clause signatures), and general circuit structures for implementing 3AND gates and conjunctions using CCNOTs.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical reduction from SAT to UNIQUE SAT. It then details the construction of the filtered oracle by rewriting the indicator function into a system of linear equations over $\mathbb{F}_2$, which is finally implemented via complex quantum circuits involving ancilla qubits and CCNOT gates.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges abstract complexity theory (NP-completeness) with concrete proposals for nonlinear quantum computation, offering a pathway to solving hard problems using physical models like BECs that exhibit such nonlinearities.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Valiant-Vazirani filter. (a) Illustration of the set {0, 1}n containing all n-bit strings x, shown as points. Points marked black (chosen randomly) indicate s satisfying assignments with f(x) = 1. In this example, n = 10 and s = 9. (b) Random partition into 2k subsets for different values of k. For each k, the individual sectors can be indexed by a number a ∈{0, 1}k (not shown in the illustration). When s ≈2k there is, on average, 1 satisfying assignment per circular sector. In the example shown, this occurs when k = 3.
Figure 3: Circuits to implement the 8 clause signatures. Here a, b, c ∈{0, 1} and X is a σx gate. The 3AND gate is defined in Figure 4.
Figure 5: Circuit to implement M-bit conjunction using CCNOTs. Here xi ∈{0, 1}. This requires O(M) CCNOT gates and O(M) additional ancilla initialized to |0⟩. The case M = 5 is shown.
